title: Crossnacreevy Weather
text: crossmet provides tools importing, summarising visualising daily meteorological observations AFBI Crossnacreevy weather station Northern Ireland. package reads annual worksheets Excel workbook, reshapes observations tidy long-format data frame, produces year-specific monthly summaries long-term monthly climate summaries, creates weather plots.

title: Crossnacreevy Weather
text: Install development version GitHub: ```r install.packages(“pak”) pak::pak(“GABurns/crossmet”) ```

title: Crossnacreevy Weather
text: `ImportWeather()` reads worksheets needed requested date range. Worksheets expected named four-digit year (example, `2023`) follow Crossnacreevy workbook layout. ```r library(crossmet) weather <- ImportWeather( file = “data/crossnacreevy_weather.xlsx”, start_date = “2020-01-01”, end_date = “2024-12-31” ) head(weather) ``` returned data frame contains `Date`, `DOY`, `variable` `value` columns, one row per date weather variable.

title: Crossnacreevy Weather
text: `MonthlySummaryTable()` calculates monthly values separately year. Rainfall daily solar-radiation totals summed; daily maximum temperature represented monthly maximum; daily minimum temperature monthly minimum; variables monthly mean. ```r yearly_months <- MonthlySummaryTable(weather) ``` `ClimateSummaryTable()` calculates long-term monthly climatological values. first calculates relevant monthly statistic year, averages yearly monthly values across available years. means rainfall climatology mean annual monthly rainfall totals, rather average daily rainfall. ```r climate_normals <- ClimateSummaryTable(weather) ``` Missing observations excluded calculations. yearly monthly statistic `NA` group observed values; climatological average `NA` years missing month variable.

title: Crossnacreevy Weather
text: plotting functions return ggplot objects can customised normal ggplot2 layers. ```r PlotMonthlyGrid(weather, variable = “RH (%)”) RainfallPlot(weather) TemperaturePlot(weather) ``` save selection plots monthly grid plots: ```r saved_files <- SaveWeatherPlots( weather, plots = c(“temperature”, “rainfall”, “relative_humidity”), monthly_grids = TRUE, path = “outputs/weather-plots” ) saved_files ``` function returns paths files creates, including monthly grid images.

title: Crossnacreevy Weather
text: worksheet represents one calendar year named using year. workbook contains two header rows followed daily observations. expected weather columns Date, DOY, minimum maximum temperature, mean air temperature, temperature difference, rainfall, soil temperatures, average wind speed, relative humidity, leaf wetness daily solar radiation. Date values must readable readxl Excel dates. See function help pages complete argument details: ```r ?ImportWeather ?MonthlySummaryTable ?ClimateSummaryTable ?PlotMonthlyGrid ?SaveWeatherPlots ```

title: Crossnacreevy Weather
text: Run package tests : ```r pak::pak(“GABurns/crossmet”) testthat::test_local() ``` package uses testthat edition 3.

title: Monthly Climate Summary Table — ClimateSummaryTable
text: Calculates long-term monthly climatological summaries across years. Daily observations first summarised within calendar year: rainfall solar radiation summed, daily maximum minimum temperatures represented monthly maxima minima, variables represented monthly means. resulting yearly monthly values averaged across years.

title: Monthly Climate Summary Table — ClimateSummaryTable
text: data data frame containing Date, variable, value columns.

title: Monthly Climate Summary Table — ClimateSummaryTable
text: tibble one row per variable one column per calendar month. Years non-missing observations month-variable combination excluded climatological average; years missing, result NA.

title: Import weather data from Excel — ImportWeather
text: Imports weather data Excel workbook individual worksheets contain data separate years. worksheets required cover requested date range imported. resulting data combined, filtered requested dates, converted long format. Excel workbook expected contain following columns: `date`, `DOY`, `Temperature deg C`, `Air temp`, `Temp diff`, `Rainfall`, `Soil 15cm`, `Soil 45cm`, `Average Wind`, `RH`, `Leaf`, `Lite totals`. Worksheet names expected contain four-digit year, example `"2023"`, `"2024"`, `"2025"`.

title: Import weather data from Excel — ImportWeather
Import weather data from Excel — ImportWeather
text: file Character string. Path Excel workbook containing weather data. start_date Start date period import. Either `Date` object character string can converted date using `.Date()`, e.g. `"2023-01-01"`. end_date End date period import. Either `Date` object character string can converted date using `.Date()`, e.g. `"2025-12-31"`.

title: Import weather data from Excel — ImportWeather
text: tibble long format four columns: date Observation date. DOY Day year. variable Weather variable measured. value Observed value.

title: Import weather data from Excel — ImportWeather
text: worksheets corresponding years `start_date` `end_date` read. example, request `"2023-06-01"` `"2025-04-30"` attempt read 2023, 2024 2025 worksheets. worksheets combined, observations outside requested date range removed.
